# Sirach Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Sirach 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/SIR_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Do not become an enemy where you were a friend, for a bad name brings shame and reproach — so it is with the double-tongued person.

**2** Do not put your confidence in your own counsel, lest it tear you apart like a bull.

**3** Your leaves will be devoured and your fruit destroyed, and you will be left like a withered tree.

**4** An evil soul destroys the one who has it and makes it a mockery to its enemies.

**5** A pleasant manner wins many friends, and an agreeable tongue attracts many greetings.

**6** Let those who wish you well be many, but let one in a thousand be your counselor.

**7** If you want to make a friend, test him first and do not trust him too quickly.

**8** For some are friends only for their own convenience, and will not stand by you in the day of trouble.

**9** Some turn from friends into enemies and will expose your quarrel to your disgrace.

**10** Some are companions at the table, but will not be found when trouble comes.

**11** While things go well for you, such a person will be like another self and make free with your servants.

**12** But if you are brought low, he will turn against you and will vanish from your sight.

**13** Separate yourself from your enemies and be wary with your friends.

**14** A faithful friend is a secure fortress; whoever finds one has found a treasure.

**15** There is nothing so precious as a faithful friend; his worth cannot be weighed.

**16** A faithful friend is a life-giving medicine; those who fear the Lord will find one for themselves.

**17** One who fears the Lord cultivates true friendship, for as the person is, so too is his companion.

**18** My child, from your youth accept instruction, and until your hair is white you will keep finding wisdom.

**19** Come to her like a farmer who plows and sows, and wait for her good harvest; for you will toil briefly in cultivating her, and soon you will eat of her produce.

**20** How harsh she seems to the undisciplined! The foolish person cannot endure her.

**21** She will weigh heavily on him like a stone of testing, and it will not be long before he throws her off.

**22** For wisdom lives up to her name; she is not accessible to many.

**23** Listen, my child, and accept my judgment; do not reject what I advise.

**24** Put your feet into her fetters and your neck into her collar.

**25** Bend your shoulder to bear her and do not chafe under her bonds.

**26** Come to her with all your soul, and follow her ways with all your strength.

**27** Search for her, pursue her, and seek her out; she will make herself known to you. When you have taken hold of her, do not let go.

**28** For in the end you will find the rest she offers, and she will be changed into your delight.

**29** Her fetters will become for you a strong defense, and her collar a splendid robe.

**30** Her ornament is of gold; her bonds are a cord of blue.

**31** You will wear her as a robe of glory, and put her on as a garland of celebration.

**32** If you are willing, my child, you can be educated; if you are diligent, you will succeed.

**33** If you love to listen, you will receive instruction; if you give your attention, you will become wise.

**34** Stand in the company of the elders; and whenever you find someone wise, attach yourself to him.

**35** Be glad to hear every discourse about godliness, and do not let a wise saying pass you by.

**36** If you see a discerning person, go to him early; let your feet wear out his threshold.

**37** Reflect on the ordinances of the Lord and give your mind to his commandments; he himself will instruct your mind, and your desire for wisdom will be fulfilled.
